task_description:
# Expose an Ash knowledge base over a strict JSON:API HTTP interface

## Background

`/home/user/kbapi` is an Elixir project (OTP app `:kbapi`, Elixir 1.18.4 / OTP 27.3.4) built on **Ash Framework 3.31** with **ash_json_api 1.7**, `plug` and `open_api_spex` already declared as dependencies and pre-compiled offline.

The project already contains a working data layer and nothing else:

- `Kbapi.Knowledge` — the Ash domain, listing all five resources.
- `Kbapi.Knowledge.Author` — `name`, `handle`, `bio`, `role` (`:reader | :editor | :admin`), `has_many :articles`.
- `Kbapi.Knowledge.Article` — `title` (required, min length 3), `slug` (required), `body`, `status` (`:draft | :published | :archived`, default `:draft`), `rank` (integer, default 0), `word_count` (integer, default 0); `belongs_to :author` (writable), `has_many :comments`, `many_to_many :tags` through `Kbapi.Knowledge.ArticleTag`; a public `comment_count` count aggregate.
- `Kbapi.Knowledge.Tag` — `name`, `slug`, `many_to_many :articles`.
- `Kbapi.Knowledge.Comment` — `body` (required, min length 2), `approved` (boolean, default `false`), `belongs_to :article` (writable).
- `Kbapi.Knowledge.Fixtures` — deterministic seed data plus `reset!/0` and the `author_id/1`, `article_id/1`, `tag_id/1`, `comment_id/1` lookup helpers. **Do not modify this module.**

All resources use `Ash.DataLayer.Ets` with `private? true`, so every process has its own isolated store.

There is no HTTP layer at all. Build one.

## Requirements

Build a JSON:API-conformant HTTP interface over these resources, mounted at `/api`, together with the authorization and content-negotiation behaviour described below. Every requirement is stated as observable request/response behaviour; how you get there is up to you.

### Entry point

- `Kbapi.Api.Endpoint` must be a `Plug` (it must export `init/1` and `call/2`). The verifier builds requests with `Plug.Test.conn/2,3` and invokes `Kbapi.Api.Endpoint.call(conn, Kbapi.Api.Endpoint.init([]))` **in the calling process** — no network listener is started and none may be required.
- `Kbapi.Api.Router` must be the JSON:API router module that `Kbapi.Api.Endpoint` serves under the `/api` path prefix.
- Every JSON:API response must be sent with the `application/vnd.api+json` content type and must be a JSON:API document: successful documents carry the top-level `jsonapi` member `{"version": "1.0"}` and a top-level `links.self` equal to the requested absolute URL; `self`/`related` links are absolute URLs derived from the request plus the `/api` prefix.

### JSON:API resource types

`Article` is `"article"`, `Author` is `"author"`, `Tag` is `"tag"`, `Comment` is `"comment"`. `ArticleTag` is not exposed.

### Routes (all paths below are relative to the `/api` prefix)

Articles, under the base path `/articles`:

| Method | Path | Behaviour |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GET | `/articles` | collection of articles |
| GET | `/articles/:id` | one article |
| POST | `/articles` | create an article |
| PATCH | `/articles/:id` | update an article |
| DELETE | `/articles/:id` | destroy an article |
| PATCH | `/articles/:id/publish` | run the article `:publish` action |
| GET | `/articles/:id/comments` | the article's comments, as full `comment` resource objects |
| GET | `/articles/:id/relationships/tags` | the article's tag linkage |
| POST | `/articles/:id/relationships/tags` | add the supplied tags to the article |
| PATCH | `/articles/:id/relationships/tags` | replace the article's tags with the supplied tags |
| DELETE | `/articles/:id/relationships/tags` | remove the supplied tags from the article |
| POST | `/articles/reindex` | run the article `:reindex` generic action |
| GET | `/articles/tally/:status` | run the article `:tally` generic action |

Other collections:

| Method | Path | Behaviour |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GET | `/authors`, `/authors/:id` | author collection / member |
| POST | `/authors` | create an author |
| PATCH | `/authors/:id` | update an author |
| GET | `/authors/:id/articles` | that author's articles, as full `article` resource objects |
| GET | `/tags`, `/tags/:id` | tag collection / member |
| GET | `/comments`, `/comments/:id` | comment collection / member |
| POST | `/comments` | create a comment |
| DELETE | `/comments/:id` | destroy a comment |
| GET | `/feed` | keyset-paginated article feed (see below) |
| GET | `/moderation/comments/pending` | comments whose `approved` is `false` |
| PATCH | `/moderation/comments/:id/approve` | run the comment `:approve` action |
| GET | `/open_api` | OpenAPI 3.0.0 document for the whole API |
| GET | `/json_schema` | JSON schema document for the whole API |

### Article representation

- By default an `article` resource object's `attributes` member contains exactly `title`, `slug`, `body`, `status`, `rank`, `word_count` and `author_id`. `comment_count` is **not** rendered by default but must be selectable via a sparse fieldset (`?fields[article]=title,comment_count`), which must also restrict the rendered attributes to exactly what was requested.
- The `author` relationship must always carry its resource-identifier `data` member, even when the caller does not ask for it. `tags` and `comments` must **not** carry a `data` member unless the caller requests them via `include`.
- An article resource object must carry a `links.self` pointing at its own `GET /api/articles/:id` route, `relationships.comments.links.related` pointing at `GET /api/articles/:id/comments`, and `relationships.tags.links.self` pointing at `GET /api/articles/:id/relationships/tags`.
- The includable relationship paths for `article` are `author`, `author.articles`, `tags` and `comments`; the includable path for `comment` is `article`, and for `author` it is `articles`. Any other `include` value must be rejected with HTTP 400 and error `code` `"invalid_includes"` and `source.parameter` `"include"`.

### Querying

- `GET /api/articles` must support `sort` (including the `-` descending prefix) over the article's own attributes, and must reject an unknown sort field with HTTP 400, error `code` `"invalid_sort"` and `source.parameter` `"sort"`.
- `GET /api/articles` must support filtering on its own attributes (`filter[status]=published`), on a related resource's attributes (`filter[author][handle]=ada`) and with comparison operators (`filter[word_count][greater_than]=500`). Filtering on a field that does not exist must produce HTTP 400.
- `GET /api/articles` must be offset-paginated: `?page[limit]=2` returns two records, reports `meta.page` as `{"limit": 2, "offset": 0}`, sets `links.prev` to `null` and provides a `links.next` that carries `page[offset]=2`; following that link returns the next window and reports `meta.page` as `{"limit": 2, "offset": 2}`.
- `GET /api/tags` must **ignore** `filter` and `sort` query parameters entirely (it must answer 200 with the full unsorted collection rather than filtering, sorting or erroring).

### `/api/feed`

- Serves articles through a dedicated `Kbapi.Knowledge.Article` read action named `:feed` that is **keyset**-paginated only (offset paging must not be available on it), always paginates, and defaults to a page size of 2.
- Results are ordered by `rank` descending, then by `id` ascending.
- `meta.page` reports only the effective `{"limit": n}`; `links.next` carries a `page[after]=<cursor>` parameter, and following it returns the next window. On the last page `links.next` is `null`.
- `?page[limit]=3` returns three records.
- A cursor that is not a valid keyset must be rejected with HTTP 400 and error `code` `"invalid_keyset"`.

### Writes and error documents

- `POST /api/articles` accepts `title`, `slug`, `body`, `status`, `rank`, `word_count` and `author_id` and answers HTTP 201 with the created resource object.
- A create/update request body whose `data` member has no `type` must be rejected with HTTP 400 and error `code` `"missing_type"` and `source.pointer` `"/data"`.
- A missing required attribute must produce HTTP 400 with error `code` `"required"`, `title` `"Required"` and `source.pointer` `"/data/attributes/<attribute>"`.
- An attribute that violates a constraint must produce HTTP 400 with error `code` `"invalid_attribute"` and `source.pointer` `"/data/attributes/<attribute>"`.
- An attribute the action does not accept must produce HTTP 400 with error `code` `"invalid_body"` and `source.pointer` `"/data/attributes/<attribute>"`.
- `PATCH /api/articles/:id` accepts `title`, `body`, `status`, `rank` and `word_count`, and must additionally accept a `tags` member inside `data.relationships` (a JSON:API to-many linkage array) which **replaces** the article's tags.
- `DELETE /api/articles/:id` answers HTTP 200 with the destroyed resource object.
- The three `/articles/:id/relationships/tags` mutation routes each answer HTTP 200 with the article's resulting tag linkage — a `data` array of resource identifier objects that contain **only** `type` and `id`. A body whose `data` is not an array must be rejected with HTTP 400, error `code` `"invalid_body"` and `source.pointer` `"/data"`; a linkage entry naming a tag that does not exist must produce HTTP 404 with error `code` `"not_found"`.
- Requesting a member that does not exist (e.g. `GET /api/articles/<unknown-uuid>`) must produce HTTP 404 with error `code` `"not_found"`.

### Article actions to add

- `:publish` — an update action reachable at `PATCH /api/articles/:id/publish` that sets `status` to `:published`. If the article's stored `status` is already `:archived` the request must fail with HTTP 400, error `code` `"invalid_attribute"`, `source.pointer` `"/data/attributes/status"` and `detail` exactly `cannot publish an archived article`, and the record must be left untouched.
- `:reindex` — a generic action reachable at `POST /api/articles/reindex` whose HTTP 201 response body is exactly a JSON object with the keys `indexed` (total number of `Article` records), `published` (number whose `status` is `:published`) and `words` (sum of `word_count` over all articles), and nothing else.
- `:tally` — a generic action reachable at `GET /api/articles/tally/:status` that takes the status as a path parameter and answers HTTP 200 with the body `{"result": <number of articles with that status>}`. Supplying the same argument in both the path and the query string must be rejected with HTTP 400 and error `code` `"invalid_query"`; a status outside the allowed set must be rejected with HTTP 400, error `code` `"invalid_argument"` and `source.pointer` `"/data/attributes/status"`.

### Comment actions to add

- `:pending` — a read action reachable at `GET /api/moderation/comments/pending` returning only comments whose `approved` is `false`.
- `:approve` — an update action reachable at `PATCH /api/moderation/comments/:id/approve` that sets `approved` to `true`.

### Actor resolution and authorization

- The request header `x-actor-handle` names the calling actor. Its value must be matched against `Kbapi.Knowledge.Author`'s `handle`; the matching author becomes the Ash actor for the request. A request without the header is anonymous.
- If the header is present but no author has that handle, the request must be answered with HTTP 401, content type `application/vnd.api+json`, and a body that is exactly:

  ```json
  {"errors": [{"code": "unknown_actor", "status": "401", "title": "Unauthorized", "detail": "unknown actor handle <handle>"}]}
  ```

  where `<handle>` is the header value. No Ash action may run for such a request.
- Authorization must be enforced on every request:
  - Reading articles, authors, tags and comments is allowed for everyone, including anonymous callers.
  - Creating, updating, destroying, publishing and mutating the tag linkage of an article requires an actor whose `role` is `:editor` or `:admin`.
  - `:reindex` requires an actor whose `role` is `:admin`.
  - `:tally` is allowed for everyone.
  - Creating a comment is allowed for everyone; updating (including `:approve`) and destroying a comment requires an actor whose `role` is `:editor` or `:admin`.
  - Authors and tags need no authorization.
- Every denial must produce HTTP 403 with error `code` `"forbidden"`, and must not change any stored data.

### Content negotiation and unmatched routes

- An `Accept` header of `application/vnd.api+json; charset=utf-8` must be rejected with HTTP 406 and error `code` `"unacceptable_media_type"`.
- A request body sent with `Content-Type: application/json` must be rejected with HTTP 415 and error `code` `"unsupported_media_type"`.
- A path under `/api` that matches no route must produce HTTP 404 with error `code` `"no_route_found"`.
- A path outside `/api` that matches nothing must be answered by `Kbapi.Api.Endpoint` itself with HTTP 404, content type `application/vnd.api+json`, and a body that is exactly:

  ```json
  {"errors": [{"code": "not_found", "status": "404", "title": "NotFound", "detail": "no route found"}]}
  ```

## Implementation Hints

- Project path: `/home/user/kbapi`
- `mix compile` must succeed with no errors; the verifier runs the project with `mix run` under `MIX_ENV=dev` and no network access, so do not add dependencies.
- Do not edit `lib/kbapi/knowledge/fixtures.ex`, and do not change the attribute names, types, defaults, constraints or relationship names of the existing resources; the verifier relies on them and on `Kbapi.Knowledge.Fixtures.reset!/0`.
- Keep all new modules under `lib/`; `Kbapi.Api.Router` and `Kbapi.Api.Endpoint` are the only module names the verifier references directly.
task_integrations: - None (Ash Framework, ash_json_api, Plug and the ETS data layer all run locally in-process; the environment has no network access at solve or verify time.)

# Verification Plan

## Setup

1. `cd /home/user/kbapi`
2. Write a self-contained ExUnit driver script to `/tmp/harbor_jsonapi_test.exs` and run it with `mix run /tmp/harbor_jsonapi_test.exs` (MIX_ENV=dev). The script defines an in-line ExUnit formatter that prints one `@@HARBOR@@<test name>@@<status>@@<base64 failure detail>` line per test, declares the suite below, and calls `ExUnit.run/0`.
3. Every scenario calls `Kbapi.Knowledge.Fixtures.reset!/0` in an ExUnit `setup` block first. Because the resources use ETS with `private? true`, each test process starts from an empty store and the fixtures are re-seeded per scenario.
4. All HTTP requests are built with `Plug.Test.conn/2,3` (default host `www.example.com`), given the `accept` header `application/vnd.api+json` (and, when a body is sent, the `content-type` header `application/vnd.api+json`), and dispatched with `Kbapi.Api.Endpoint.call(conn, Kbapi.Api.Endpoint.init([]))`. Any raised exception is caught and reported as a failure. Reference `Kbapi.Api.Endpoint` through `Module.concat/1` so the suite still compiles against an unsolved project.

## Fixture data (seeded by `Kbapi.Knowledge.Fixtures.reset!/0`)

- Authors: `ada` (Ada Lovelace, role `:editor`), `bob` (Bob Reader, role `:reader`), `cleo` (Cleo Root, role `:admin`).
- Tags: `elixir`, `otp`, `web`.
- Articles: `elixir-basics` (published, rank 30, word_count 1200, author ada, tags elixir+otp), `otp-supervisors` (published, rank 20, word_count 800, author ada, tag otp), `web-drafts` (draft, rank 10, word_count 300, author cleo, tag web), `archived-notes` (archived, rank 40, word_count 50, author bob, no tags).
- Comments: `first` (approved, on elixir-basics), `second` (pending, on elixir-basics), `third` (pending, on otp-supervisors).
- Ids are obtained through `Fixtures.author_id/1`, `Fixtures.article_id/1`, `Fixtures.tag_id/1` and `Fixtures.comment_id/1` with the atom keys `:ada | :bob | :cleo`, `:elixir | :otp | :web`, `:elixir_basics | :otp_supervisors | :web_drafts | :archived_notes`, `:first | :second | :third`.

## Verification Steps

1. **T01 index** — `GET /api/articles` returns 200 with four `data` entries, all of `type` `"article"`, whose ids are exactly the four fixture article ids.
2. **T02 document envelope** — the same request has response content type `application/vnd.api+json`, body `jsonapi` equal to `{"version": "1.0"}` and `links.self` equal to `http://www.example.com/api/articles`.
3. **T03 default attributes** — `GET /api/articles/<elixir_basics>` returns 200 and `data.attributes` has exactly the keys `title, slug, body, status, rank, word_count, author_id`, with `title` `"Elixir Basics"`, `status` `"published"`, `rank` `30`.
4. **T04 always-on linkage** — for the same request `data.relationships.author.data` equals `{"type": "author", "id": <ada>}`, while `relationships.tags` and `relationships.comments` have no `data` key.
5. **T05 links** — for the same request `data.links.self` is `http://www.example.com/api/articles/<id>`, `relationships.comments.links.related` is `http://www.example.com/api/articles/<id>/comments` and `relationships.tags.links.self` is `http://www.example.com/api/articles/<id>/relationships/tags`.
6. **T06 sparse fieldset** — `GET /api/articles/<elixir_basics>?fields[article]=title,comment_count` returns `data.attributes` exactly `{"title": "Elixir Basics", "comment_count": 2}`.
7. **T07 sort** — `?sort=-rank` yields slugs `[archived-notes, elixir-basics, otp-supervisors, web-drafts]` and `?sort=rank` yields the reverse.
8. **T08 invalid sort** — `?sort=nope` returns 400, error `code` `"invalid_sort"`, `status` `"400"`, `source.parameter` `"sort"`.
9. **T09 attribute filter** — `?filter[status]=published&sort=rank` yields slugs `[otp-supervisors, elixir-basics]`.
10. **T10 relationship filter** — `?filter[author][handle]=ada&sort=rank` yields slugs `[otp-supervisors, elixir-basics]`.
11. **T11 operator filter** — `?filter[word_count][greater_than]=500&sort=rank` yields slugs `[otp-supervisors, elixir-basics]`.
12. **T12 unknown filter field** — `?filter[nope]=1` returns 400 with an `errors` array.
13. **T13 include tags** — `?include=tags` returns 200; `included` holds exactly the three tag ids and every entry has `type` `"tag"`; the `elixir-basics` entry's `relationships.tags.data` holds the `elixir` and `otp` tag ids.
14. **T14 multi-hop include** — `GET /api/articles/<elixir_basics>?include=author.articles` returns 200 and `included` contains both `author` and `article` entries, including author `ada` and article `otp-supervisors`.
15. **T15 invalid include** — `?include=nope` returns 400, error `code` `"invalid_includes"`, `source.parameter` `"include"`.
16. **T16 offset page 1** — `?sort=rank&page[limit]=2` yields slugs `[web-drafts, otp-supervisors]`, `meta.page` `{"limit": 2, "offset": 0}`, `links.prev` `null` and a `links.next` containing `page[offset]=2`.
17. **T17 offset page 2** — following that `links.next` yields slugs `[elixir-basics, archived-notes]` and `meta.page` `{"limit": 2, "offset": 2}`.
18. **T18 feed page 1** — `GET /api/feed` returns slugs `[archived-notes, elixir-basics]`, `meta.page` `{"limit": 2}` and a `links.next` containing `page[after]=`.
19. **T19 feed page 2** — following it returns slugs `[otp-supervisors, web-drafts]` and `links.next` `null`.
20. **T20 bad cursor** — `GET /api/feed?page[after]=not-a-cursor` returns 400 with error `code` `"invalid_keyset"`.
21. **T21 feed limit** — `GET /api/feed?page[limit]=3` returns slugs `[archived-notes, elixir-basics, otp-supervisors]` and `meta.page` `{"limit": 3}`.
22. **T22 unknown member** — `GET /api/articles/00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000` returns 404 with error `code` `"not_found"` and `status` `"404"`.
23. **T23 tag query params ignored** — `GET /api/tags?filter[slug]=otp&sort=slug` returns 200 with all three tags.
24. **T24 create** — `POST /api/articles` as `ada` with attributes `title` `"Streams"`, `slug` `"streams"`, `body` `"Lazy enumerables."`, `word_count` `640`, `author_id` `<ada>` returns 201 with `data.type` `"article"`, `slug` `"streams"`, `status` `"draft"`, `rank` `0`; a subsequent `GET /api/articles` returns five entries.
25. **T25 required** — the same POST without `title` returns 400 with error `code` `"required"`, `title` `"Required"`, `source.pointer` `"/data/attributes/title"`.
26. **T26 constraint** — the same POST with `title` `"ab"` returns 400 with error `code` `"invalid_attribute"`, `source.pointer` `"/data/attributes/title"` and `meta.min` `3`.
27. **T27 unaccepted attribute** — the same POST with an extra `"bogus": 1` attribute returns 400 with error `code` `"invalid_body"` and `source.pointer` `"/data/attributes/bogus"`.
28. **T28 missing type** — the same POST with `data` lacking `type` returns 400 with error `code` `"missing_type"` and `source.pointer` `"/data"`.
29. **T29 create forbidden** — the same POST as `bob` and as an anonymous caller both return 403 with error `code` `"forbidden"`, and `GET /api/articles` still returns four entries.
30. **T30 patch** — `PATCH /api/articles/<web_drafts>` as `ada` with `title` `"Web Drafts v2"` and `rank` `55` returns 200 with those values, and a subsequent `GET` confirms the title.
31. **T31 patch relationships** — `PATCH /api/articles/<elixir_basics>` as `ada` with `data.relationships.tags.data` `[{"type": "tag", "id": <web>}]` returns 200, and `GET /api/articles/<elixir_basics>/relationships/tags` then returns exactly `[<web>]`.
32. **T32 publish** — `PATCH /api/articles/<web_drafts>/publish` as `ada` returns 200 with `status` `"published"`, confirmed by a subsequent `GET`.
33. **T33 publish archived** — `PATCH /api/articles/<archived_notes>/publish` as `ada` returns 400 with error `code` `"invalid_attribute"`, `detail` `"cannot publish an archived article"`, `source.pointer` `"/data/attributes/status"`, and the article's `status` is still `"archived"`.
34. **T34 delete** — `DELETE /api/articles/<archived_notes>` as `bob` returns 403; as `ada` it returns 200 with `data.id` equal to that id, and a subsequent `GET` on it returns 404.
35. **T35 related comments** — `GET /api/articles/<elixir_basics>/comments` returns 200 with the `first` and `second` comment ids, all of `type` `"comment"` and each carrying an `attributes` member.
36. **T36 relationship linkage** — `GET /api/articles/<elixir_basics>/relationships/tags` returns 200 with the `elixir` and `otp` tag ids, and each `data` entry has exactly the keys `id` and `type`.
37. **T37 post to relationship** — `POST /api/articles/<otp_supervisors>/relationships/tags` as `ada` with `[{"type": "tag", "id": <web>}]` returns 200 whose `data` holds the `otp` and `web` ids, confirmed by a subsequent linkage `GET`.
38. **T38 patch relationship** — `PATCH /api/articles/<elixir_basics>/relationships/tags` as `ada` with `[{"type": "tag", "id": <web>}]` returns 200 with `data` exactly `[<web>]`, confirmed by a subsequent linkage `GET`.
39. **T39 delete from relationship** — `DELETE /api/articles/<elixir_basics>/relationships/tags` as `ada` with `[{"type": "tag", "id": <otp>}]` returns 200 with `data` exactly `[<elixir>]`, confirmed by a subsequent linkage `GET`.
40. **T40 relationship errors** — a POST whose `data` is a single object (not an array) returns 400 with error `code` `"invalid_body"` and `source.pointer` `"/data"`; a POST naming tag id `00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000` returns 404 with error `code` `"not_found"`; a PATCH as `bob` returns 403.
41. **T41 reindex** — `POST /api/articles/reindex` as `cleo` returns 201 with the body exactly `{"indexed": 4, "published": 2, "words": 2350}`.
42. **T42 reindex authorization** — the same request as `ada` and as an anonymous caller both return 403 with error `code` `"forbidden"`.
43. **T43 tally** — `GET /api/articles/tally/published` returns 200 with body `{"result": 2}` and `/tally/draft` returns `{"result": 1}`; `/tally/published?status=draft` returns 400 with error `code` `"invalid_query"`; `/tally/nope` returns 400 with error `code` `"invalid_argument"` and `source.pointer` `"/data/attributes/status"`.
44. **T44 pending comments** — `GET /api/moderation/comments/pending` returns 200 with exactly the `second` and `third` comment ids.
45. **T45 approve** — `PATCH /api/moderation/comments/<second>/approve` as `bob` returns 403; as `ada` it returns 200 with `attributes.approved` `true`, after which the pending list holds only the `third` comment id.
46. **T46 author articles** — `GET /api/authors/<ada>/articles?sort=rank` returns 200 with slugs `[otp-supervisors, elixir-basics]`, all of `type` `"article"`.
47. **T47 anonymous comment** — `POST /api/comments` with no actor header, body `"Drive by"` and `article_id` `<otp_supervisors>` returns 201 with `attributes.approved` `false`, and `GET /api/comments` then returns four entries.
48. **T48 unknown actor** — `GET /api/articles` with header `x-actor-handle: nobody` returns 401 and the body is exactly `{"errors": [{"code": "unknown_actor", "status": "401", "title": "Unauthorized", "detail": "unknown actor handle nobody"}]}`.
49. **T49 media types** — `GET /api/articles` with `accept: application/vnd.api+json; charset=utf-8` returns 406 with error `code` `"unacceptable_media_type"`; a `POST /api/articles` as `ada` sent with `content-type: application/json` returns 415 with error `code` `"unsupported_media_type"`.
50. **T50 unmatched routes** — `GET /api/nothing-here` returns 404 with error `code` `"no_route_found"`; `GET /nothing-here` returns 404 and the body is exactly `{"errors": [{"code": "not_found", "status": "404", "title": "NotFound", "detail": "no route found"}]}`.
51. **T51 open api** — `GET /api/open_api` returns 200 with `openapi` `"3.0.0"` and `paths` containing at least `/api/articles`, `/api/articles/{id}`, `/api/articles/{id}/publish`, `/api/articles/{id}/comments`, `/api/articles/{id}/relationships/tags`, `/api/articles/reindex`, `/api/articles/tally/{status}`, `/api/feed`, `/api/authors/{id}/articles`, `/api/moderation/comments/pending`, `/api/moderation/comments/{id}/approve`.
52. **T52 json schema** — `GET /api/json_schema` returns 200 with top-level `links` and `definitions` members.
